title: Dividend investing in 2026: 5 stocks to know | Stock Market News
text:

Dividend stocks provide stability to investors’ portfolios during the volatile periods in the stock market.

The stability of these stocks has proven the importance of dividends to investors time and again.

Dividends also provide an incentive for companies to increase their earnings, so they can pay an even higher dividend next year. This attracts more investors, which takes the company’s share price higher.

This is why, all else being equal, dividend-paying stocks tend to deliver higher returns than non-dividend-paying stocks over the long term.

Even the father of value investing Benjamin Graham agreed when he said: ‘The true investor will do better if he forgets about the stock market and pays attention to his dividend returns and to the operation results of his companies.’

With that, here are five stocks that you should have on your dividend watchlist for 2026…

ITC is a diversified conglomerate with businesses spanning fast moving consumer goods, hotels, paperboards and packaging, agri-business, and IT. The company is the country's leading FMCG firm and the market leader in the Indian paperboard and packaging industry.

In the agri sector, it's acknowledged globally as a pioneer in farmer empowerment through its wide-reaching agri business. In the hotels segment, it's a pre-eminent hotel chain in India.

For years, ITC was planning to gradually shift towards an asset-light model in the hospitality sector for further expansion. This was put to action with the hotel business demerger.

Over the last decade, ITC has successfully created an array of strong brands which are either #1 or #2. They are market leaders in their respective categories.

The stock has always been considered as an attractive dividend play. Right from humble beginnings in 1994, the company has rewarded investors with a higher payout compared to its peers.

Over the years, the company's management has laid out a flexible capital allocation policy. It has said that dividend payouts will be stepped up to about 80-85% of its post-tax profits.

In FY24, ITC paid out ₹14.5 per share as dividends. ITC has been paying dividends since 1994 without missing a single year in between. The dividend payout ratio in FY26 was 86.4%. The company's 5-year average dividend payout ratio is 90.28%.

Hindustan Aeronautics manufactures and maintains aircraft and helicopters for the Indian Airforce, Indian Army, ISRO, Indian Navy, and Indian Coast Guard, among others.

Defence stocks in India have garnered significant investor interest. The sector has surpassed a significant milestone of ₹1 trillion in the total value of defence production.

HAL plays a strategic role in India's defence program being the only Indian company having specialisation in aircraft manufacturing, maintenance, and related services.

Along with Saffran (SAFHAL) the company is developing a new helicopter engine called Aravalli.

The company also has a massive procurement order worth ₹26000 crore for 240 aero engines for Su-30 MKI aircraft. HAL's has a very strong order backlog of ₹2.54 trillion (tn). This provides the company with a revenue visibility of around seven years.

Apart from this, the company has a deal on its cards with a US firm GE Aerospace for the joint production of F414 engines in India. The final contract is expected to be signed in 2027.

It has also set up a ₹210 crore Integrated Cryogenic Engine Manufacturing Facility (ICMF) that would cater to the entire rocket engine production under one roof for ISRO.

The company has paid regular dividends. In FY26, it declared a dividend of ₹45 per share, with a dividend payout ratio of 33%. The five-year average dividend payout ratio stands at 25.59%.

Dr Reddy's Laboratories is an Indian multinational pharmaceutical company based in Hyderabad. It manufactures and markets a wide range of pharmaceuticals in India and overseas.

The company's expertise spans several therapeutic areas, including oncology, gastroenterology, and cardiovascular treatments.

Dr Reddy's is actively expanding its capabilities with the recent establishment of a new oncology API facility in Vizag. This new facility aims to support the company's growing presence in the oncology sector.

Additionally, the company is making significant progress in developing biosimilars and complex generics, particularly in its biologics API division.

With nearly no debt, Dr Reddy's has shown impressive financial performance, delivering a 24.4% compound annual growth rate (CAGR) in profit over the past five years.

FY24 was an excellent year for the company. Its consolidated revenue, operating profit, and net profit increased 12%, 15%, and 24%, respectively, over FY23.

Apart from growing the core business of generics, the company invested in businesses of the future under the three spaces of consumer health, digital therapeutics, and access to novel molecules.

Dr Reddy's diversified global presence, capability, and strong balance sheet make it a partner of choice for various business partners. The company's strong balance sheet provides financial flexibility to implement all its plans.

In FY26, the company declared a dividend of ₹8 per share, with a dividend payout ratio of 16.1%.

The five-year average dividend payout ratio stands at 7.5%.

Bharat Electronics manufactures and supplies electronic equipment and systems to the defence sector. The company also has a limited presence in the civilian market. The company was formed under the Ministry of Defence to handle Indian defence electronic needs.

India's defence sector is set to witness significant growth, driven by the government's approvals of major military projects. BEL is well positioned in the procurement boom of defence electronic equipment like air defence fire control radars.

The company's strong presence in the electronics and radar systems sector makes it a crucial player in India's defence ecosystem.
